title: Generation of liver mesenchyme and ductal cell organoid co-culture
author: Dowbaj, Kohler, et al.
materials:
Timing: 15 min
10.Before starting the cell isolation, prepare all the media in advance.a.Media can be prepared ahead of time and stored in the fridge for up to 1 month (Refer to the “materials and equipment” section for media composition tables).b.Prepare 1% FBS DMEM media.11.Prepare Advanced DMEM /F12 +++ media.12.Prepare collagenase-dispase II solution (Refer to the “materials and equipment” section for media composition tables).a.Prepare the collagenase-dispase II solution immediately before use.b.Weigh collagenase and dispase immediately before adding 1% FBS DMEM.c.Warm up the solution to 37°C.
CRITICAL: This solution cannot be stored for longer than the time of the isolation experiment, as the enzymes lose activity over time when in solution.
13.During the isolation incubation times, prepare the staining solutions for flow cytometry.a.For each liver, prepare 1.5 mL staining solution with all antibodies, with 15 μL of each antibody per 1.5 mL of media.b.For the control WT liver, add 1 μL of single antibody solution per polypropylene tube per single color control with 100 μL of cell suspension.c.Prepare collection test tubes with 300 μL Advanced DMEM /F12 +++ media supplemented with ROCK inhibitor (10 μM final concentration).14.Thaw matrigel on ice at 4°C 12–18 h (overnight).

steps.title: Prepare media and reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare all media in advance (store up to 1 month at 4 °C). Make 1 % FBS DMEM, Advanced DMEM/F12+++ and collagenase‑dispase II solution (weigh collagenase and dispase, add to 1 % FBS DMEM, warm to 37 °C; use immediately). Prepare staining solutions: for each liver 1.5 mL media with 15 µL of each antibody; for WT control 1 µL antibody per tube with 100 µL cell suspension. Fill collection tubes with 300 µL Advanced DMEM/F12+++ + ROCK inhibitor (10 µM final). Thaw Matrigel on ice at 4 °C for 12–18 h (overnight).

substeps.instruction: Prepare collagenase‑dispase II solution just before use and warm to 37 °C.
Prepare 1.5 mL staining solution per liver (15 µL each antibody).
Prepare WT control staining (1 µL antibody + 100 µL cells).
Aliquot 300 µL collection tubes with ROCK inhibitor (10 µM).

steps.title: Euthanize mice and dissect liver
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice (any standard method) and dissect out the liver. Wash livers repeatedly with PBS until the supernatant is mostly clear.

steps.title: Wash and mince liver tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer livers to a petri dish, remove gallbladder, peritoneal fat and non‑liver tissue. Discard residual PBS, then chop liver into 1–2 mm pieces with scissors or a razor blade.

steps.title: Pellet tissue and wash with PBS
steps.instruction: Place tissue pieces in a tube with 10 mL PBS, let settle by gravity or spin 120 RCF for 2 min and discard supernatant. Wash pellet with 40 mL PBS by inverting, then repeat the 120 RCF/2 min spin and discard supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Settle or spin 120 RCF 2 min; discard supernatant.
Repeat spin 120 RCF 2 min; discard supernatant.

steps.title: First enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL collagenase/dispase mix (top up to ~12.5 mL) to the pellet (DNAse optional). Incubate 10 min at 37 °C water bath, pipette up/down with a 10 mL serological pipette, spin 120 RCF 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 25 mL collagenase/dispase + DNAse, incubate 90 min at 37 °C on a horizontal shaker at 130 RPM, then inspect under bright‑field microscope for presence of ducts and parenchyma.

substeps.instruction: Pipette up/down with 10 mL serological pipette.

steps.title: Repeat digestion on remaining tissue
steps.instruction: After the first digestion, carefully remove ~15 mL supernatant, then repeat steps: pipette up/down with 10 mL serological pipette, spin 120 RCF 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 25 mL collagenase/dispase + DNAse, incubate 90 min at 37 °C, 130 RPM, and re‑check digestion under the microscope.

substeps.instruction: Pipette up/down with 10 mL serological pipette.

steps.title: Wash and prepare cells for TrypLE
steps.instruction: Spin the digested suspension at 200 RCF for 5 min and discard supernatant. Wash pellet with 40 mL Advanced DMEM/F12+++ media, spin again at 200 RCF for 5 min and discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 5 mL 5×TrypLE (prepared 1:1 mix of 1× and 10× TrypLE).

steps.title: TrypLE incubation and single‑cell preparation
steps.instruction: Incubate the suspension for 10 min at 37 °C water bath. Meanwhile finish preparing pre‑conjugated antibodies for flow cytometry. After incubation, resuspend cells with a glass Pasteur pipette, examine under bright‑field microscope; if <80 % single cells repeat the 10 min 37 °C TrypLE step until >80 % single‑cell suspension is achieved.

substeps.instruction: Check single‑cell percentage; repeat TrypLE if needed.

steps.title: Stain cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL 1 % FBS DMEM media to the cell suspension, then add the staining solution prepared earlier (15 µL each antibody per 1.5 mL media for experimental liver; 1 µL antibody per tube with 100 µL cells for WT control). Incubate as required by antibody protocol.

steps.title: Filter, centrifuge and resuspend for sorting
steps.instruction: Pass the stained cell suspension through a 40 µm strainer twice. Top up with 40 mL 1 % FBS DMEM media, spin at 500 RCF for 3 min, discard supernatant, and finally resuspend the pellet in 1 mL 2 % FBS DMEM media (or appropriate blocking solution) before sorting.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend in 1 mL 2 % FBS DMEM or blocking solution.

steps.title: Flow‑cytometry sorting of mesenchyme and ductal cells
steps.instruction: Sort cells using a compatible sorter (MoFlo Legacy, Astrios, BD FACSAria, or SH800S) with recommended fluorophore combinations (e.g., Super Bright 436, GFP, APC, PE‑Cy7). Collect sorted cells into 300 µL Advanced DMEM/F12+++ containing ROCK inhibitor (10 µM). Expected yields: 10 000–40 000 mesenchymal cells and 50 000–100 000 ductal cells per mouse; viability >90 %.

steps.title: Record mouse age and expected yields
steps.instruction: Note that mice are 8–12 weeks old (heterozygous PDGFRα‑H2B‑GFP; homozygous non‑viable). Total cell yield from digestion ranges 10–80 million cells with >90 % viability. After seeding, mesenchymal cells should attach within 3 days and display fibroblast morphology (passages 0–2).

description: In Cordero-Espinoza et al.,1 we reported that when primary liver mesenchyme is co-cultured with liver ductal epithelium in 3D classical Matrigel dome, the cells fail to establish cell-cell interactions. The cells segregate in the well with the mesenchyme attaching to the plate bottom and the ductal cells forming organoids inside of the Matrigel (for reference see Figure S4M from ref. 1). Therefore, we developed two co-culture methods: a microfluidics -based method and a 2D Matrigel layer co-culture method, to enable the cell-cell interactions between both populations in vitro. The microfluidics approach facilitates the cell-cell interactions recapitulating the 3D architecture (See Figure 5 and Figure S5 from ref. 1), while the 2D-co-culture method allows more control of the ratios between cell types (See Figure 6 and Figure S6 from ref. 1) as well as it is amenable to chemical and siRNA manipulation (See Figure 7 from ref. 1). The protocol below explains the specific steps for co-culturing primary liver ductal organoids with primary liver mesenchymal cells, mainly portal fibroblasts. Both, mesenchymal cells and ductal cells can be co-cultured directly after isolation or after several sub-cultivations (2–5 passages for portal mesenchyme and any passage for ductal organoids). Notably, at the passages tested, the cells do not present any change on their phenotype following culture (for details see Figure 4D-E and Figures S4D–S4F from ref. 1). Workflows involving microfluidic cell encapsulation and co-culture protocols in Matrigel are broadly applicable to other cell types. Cells were isolated from PDGFRα-H2B-GFP mice (B6.129S4-Pdgfratm11(EGFP)Sor/J)2 which can be crossed with mTmG mice (Gt(ROSA)26Sortm4(ACTBtdTomato,-EGFP)Luo/J)3 for the easier double fluorescence labeling of the mesenchyme.
